- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.8) — reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.4) — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Avoid long-term trend extrapolation — if sentiment is flat or neutral, don’t assume sustained direction; favor short-term mean reversion.
- Correct for lagged overshoot: if model peaks 2–3 days after sentiment spike, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment is high but price is trending down, reduce forecast slope — sentiment may be overvaluing future upside.
- Don’t extrapolate beyond 10–15 days without sentiment confirmation — if sentiment drops after peak, cut forecast slope sharply.
- For 30-day horizon, cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high if sentiment is bullish — avoid overconfidence in long-term upside.
